title: Binance SEC case dropped and CZ pardon
summary: The SEC dismissed its case against Binance and Zhao with prejudice on May 29, 2025. Trump pardoned Zhao on Oct 22-23, 2025, and on 60 Minutes (Nov 2, 2025) said 'I don't know who he is'. On the All-In podcast (about Feb 2026), Zhao said he 'didn't do much' to get the pardon and that without it Binance could hardly enter the US properly. The video wrongly has Binance doing the $2B deal: MGX invested $2B in Binance, settled in USD1. Its quid-pro-quo insinuation rests on a documented sequence of events, with no proof of causation.

sub_claims.statement: The SEC lawsuit against Binance was dropped.
sub_claims.finding: The SEC, Binance and Zhao filed a joint stipulation of dismissal with prejudice on May 29, 2025 (reported May 30), ending the June 2023 civil suit. The SEC cited discretion and policy. This was separate from the 2023 DOJ guilty pleas, which stand.

sub_claims.statement: Later, Trump pardoned Binance founder Changpeng Zhao.
sub_claims.finding: Trump signed the pardon on Oct 22, 2025, and the White House announced it on Oct 23, about five months after the SEC dismissal. Leavitt called the prosecution Biden overreach with no fraud victims and said the White House Counsel reviewed the pardon.

sub_claims.statement: Binance is doing the $2 billion stablecoin deal.
sub_claims.finding: MGX (Abu Dhabi) invested $2B in Binance, announced Mar 12, 2025. On May 1, 2025, Zach Witkoff said the deal would settle in WLF's USD1. Binance was the recipient, and its CEO denies any role in choosing USD1.

sub_claims.statement: Trump said 'I don't know who he is' about Zhao.
sub_claims.finding: On CBS 60 Minutes (aired Nov 2, 2025), Trump said 'Okay, are you ready? I don't know who he is', said he didn't think he had met Zhao ('maybe I did'), and called the case a 'Biden witch hunt'.

sub_claims.statement: CZ said he didn't do anything to get the pardon but that without it Binance is severely limited in the US.
sub_claims.finding: DL News reports Zhao said on the All-In podcast (about Feb 10, 2026) that he 'didn't do much' and that 'without the pardon it's quite hard for Binance to enter the US in a proper way'. The 'UBO' and 'severely limited' lines are consistent with this but were not verified verbatim. Zhao had applied for the pardon in about May 2025.

sub_claims.statement: Implied: the USD1 investment, benefit to the Trump family and the pardon are linked ('just a couple of coincidences').
sub_claims.finding: The sequence is documented: the $2B in USD1, reports (first Bloomberg in July 2025, citing three anonymous sources, then the WSJ) that Binance wrote USD1's basic smart-contract code or helped build its technology, which Binance, Zhao ('FUD') and WLF ('factually deficient') dispute, Zhao's lobbying, then the pardon. No public evidence shows a quid pro quo, and Zhao and Binance deny any link.

corrections: Transcript says Binance is 'doing' the $2B stablecoin deal; the record shows MGX invested $2B into Binance, with the deal settled in USD1.
Transcript says Trump 'firmly denies knowing' Zhao; Trump said he didn't think he had met him and added 'maybe I did'.
The SEC dismissal (May 29, 2025) was with prejudice and also covered Zhao personally. The pardon followed on Oct 22-23, 2025.
The CZ quote comes from the All-In podcast (about Feb 2026). Its 'UBO' and 'severely limited' wording is not independently verified.

The write-up attributed the 'Binance helped build USD1' report to the WSJ alone; it originated with Bloomberg (July 2025, anonymous sources) and was later echoed by the WSJ. It is disputed by Binance, Zhao and WLF, so it is an allegation, not an established fact.
denials_and_context: White House (Leavitt): the Biden DOJ overreached, there were no fraud victims, and the White House Counsel vetted the pardon.
Trump: he was told it was a 'Biden witch hunt', he doesn't know Zhao, and his sons are in crypto.

Zhao: he did not do much to get the pardon and has no business relationship with World Liberty Financial. His lawyers threatened to sue Sen. Warren over her claim that he 'financed President Trump's stablecoin and lobbied for a pardon'.
Binance CEO Richard Teng: Binance had no role in MGX choosing USD1, and USD1 was listed elsewhere first.
The SEC civil case was separate from the 2023 criminal guilty pleas ($4.3B penalty for Binance; 4 months in prison for Zhao). Dropping the SEC case did not erase the criminal conviction.
